results.title: Unbounded family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A family $F$ of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is unbounded if no function $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ bounds every member of $F$, where $g$ bounds $f$ if there is an $N$ such that $f(n) \le g(n)$ for all $n \ge N$.

results.title: Bounding number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bounding number $\mathfrak{b}$ is the infimum of the cardinalities of all unbounded families of functions $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 18.89 for $n = 2$

results.title: Quasi-identities of groups
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A quasi-identity in $n$ unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ is a formula $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$, given by the number $n$, a finite list of premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and a conclusion $w$, all of them elements of the free group on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$.

results.title: Quasi-identities holding in a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A quasi-identity $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$ in the unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ holds in a group $G$ when every assignment of elements of $G$ to the unknowns under which each premise $w_1, \dots, w_k$ evaluates to $1$ in $G$ also makes the conclusion $w$ evaluate to $1$.

results.title: The quasivariety defined by a set of quasi-identities
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $Q$ of quasi-identities, a group $H$ belongs to the quasivariety defined by $Q$ when every quasi-identity in $Q$ holds in $H$. Every quasivariety of groups has this form.

results.title: The quasi-identities of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The quasi-theory of a group $G$ is the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. The quasivariety defined by this set is the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$.

results.title: Inclusion of quasivarieties
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sets $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ of quasi-identities, the quasivariety defined by $Q_1$ is contained in the quasivariety defined by $Q_2$: every group in which all quasi-identities of $Q_1$ hold also satisfies all quasi-identities of $Q_2$.

results.title: Maximal proper subquasivarieties
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $qG$ be the quasivariety generated by $G$, that is, the quasivariety defined by the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. A set $Q$ of quasi-identities defines a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$ when the quasivariety defined by $Q$ is contained in $qG$ but does not contain $qG$, and every quasivariety $V$ defined by a set of quasi-identities with $V$ containing the…

results.title: Budkin's problem on maximal subquasivarieties (Kourovka 14.25)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a finitely generated group $G$ such that the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$ has infinitely many maximal proper subquasivarieties: for every natural number $k$ there are sets of quasi-identities $Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1}$, each defining a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$, such that for $i \ne j$ the quasivarieties defined by $Q_i$ and $Q_j$ are different.

results.title: Some finitely generated group has infinitely many maximal subquasivarieties
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finitely generated group $G$ such that the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$ has infinitely many maximal proper subquasivarieties: for every natural number $k$ there are sets of quasi-identities $Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1}$, each defining a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$, such that for $i \ne j$ the quasivarieties defined by $Q_i$ and $Q_j$ are different.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$. An array $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ of complex numbers, indexed from $0$, is a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$ when the following hold: $S_{i,j} = 0$ whenever $i \ge 2n$ or $j \ge 2n$; $S_{i,j} = -S_{j,i}$ for all $i, j$; $S_{2n-2,\,2n-1} = 1$;…

results.title: Finite support of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{i,j} = 0$ for all $i, j$ with $i \ge 2n$ or $j \ge 2n$.

results.title: Nu-lambda Pascal matrices are skew-symmetric
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{i,j} = -S_{j,i}$ for all $i, j$.

results.title: Corner entry of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then $S_{2n-2,\,2n-1} = 1$.

results.title: Last-column recurrence of a nu-lambda Pascal matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n > 0$, let $\nu, \lambda \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $S = (S_{i,j})_{i,j \ge 0}$ be a $(\nu, \lambda)$-Pascal matrix of size $2n$ with coefficients $\beta$. Then for every $j < 2n - 2$, $S_{j,\,2n-1} = \sum_{t=0}^{N-1} \beta_t S_{j+t+1,\,2n-1}$.

results.title: The Nagell–Ljunggren cube equation for $n \equiv 5 \pmod 6$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number with $n \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. Then there are no integers $x$ and $y$ with $x \equiv 2, 3, 5$ or $6 \pmod 9$ such that $x^n - 1 = (x - 1) y^3$. Since such an $x$ is not $1$, this says that $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^3$ has no such integer solution.

results.title: The Nagell–Ljunggren cube equation for $x \equiv 2, 3, 5, 6 \pmod 9$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ be a natural number. Then there are no integers $x$ and $y$ with $x \equiv 2, 3, 5$ or $6 \pmod 9$ such that $x^n - 1 = (x - 1) y^3$. Since such an $x$ is not $1$, this says that $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^3$ has no such integer solution.

results.title: Ljunggren's theorem on the Nagell–Ljunggren equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be integers and $n$ and $q$ natural numbers with $|x| > 1$, $y > 1$, $n > 2$ and $q \ge 2$, and suppose that $x^n - 1 = (x - 1) y^q$, that is, $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^q$ (as $x \ne 1$). If $q = 2$, or $3 \mid n$, or $4 \mid n$, or $q = 3$ and $n \not\equiv 5 \pmod 6$, then $(x, y, n, q)$ is one of $(3, 11, 5, 2)$, $(7, 20, 4, 2)$, $(18, 7, 3, 3)$ and $(-19, 7, 3, 3)$.

results.title: Structure of a further solution of the Nagell–Ljunggren equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x, y, n, q$ be natural numbers with $x \ge 2$, $y \ge 2$, $n \ge 3$ and $q \ge 2$ such that $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^q$, and suppose that $(x, y, n, q)$ is none of the known solutions $(3, 11, 5, 2)$, $(7, 20, 4, 2)$ and $(18, 7, 3, 3)$. Then the least prime divisor of $n$ is at least $29$, $n$ has at most four prime factors counted with multiplicity, $n$ is prime if $q = 3$, and $n = q$ if $q \mid n$.

results.title: The Nagell–Ljunggren cube equation when $5 \mid n$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are no natural numbers $x \ge 2$, $y \ge 2$ and $n \ge 3$ with $5 \mid n$ such that $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^3$.

results.title: Dickman–de Bruijn functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function if $\rho(u) = 0$ for every real $u < 0$, $\rho$ maps $[0, \infty)$ into $[0, 1]$, $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$, $\rho(u) = 1$ for every $u \in [0, 1]$, and for every real $u > 1$ the function $\rho$ is differentiable at $u$ with $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$.

results.title: The Dickman–de Bruijn function vanishes on the negative reals
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) = 0$ for every real $u < 0$.

results.title: Range of the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $0 \le \rho(u) \le 1$ for every real $u \ge 0$.

results.title: Continuity of the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$.

results.title: The Dickman–de Bruijn function equals one on the unit interval
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) = 1$ for every $u \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Normalization of the Dickman–de Bruijn function, inequality form
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function and $u$ is a real number with $0 \le u$ and $u \le 1$, then $\rho(u) = 1$.

results.title: Differentiability of the Dickman–de Bruijn function above one
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho$ is differentiable at every real $u > 1$.

results.title: Delay differential equation of the Dickman–de Bruijn function
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$ for every real $u > 1$.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the Dickman–de Bruijn function
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) \ge 0$ for every real $u \ge 0$.

results.title: Upper bound one for the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) \le 1$ for every real $u \ge 0$.

results.title: Pointwise range bound for the Dickman–de Bruijn function
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function and $u \ge 0$ is real, then $\rho(u) \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Existence and uniqueness of the Dickman–de Bruijn function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is exactly one function $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, that is, such that $\rho(u) = 0$ for $u < 0$, $0 \le \rho(u) \le 1$ for $u \ge 0$, $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$, $\rho(u) = 1$ for $0 \le u \le 1$, and for every $u > 1$ the function $\rho$ is differentiable at $u$ with $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$.

results.title: Permutation p-value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The permutation (group-invariance) p-value of the statistic `T` at `ω`: the fraction of group elements `g` with `T (g • ω) ≥ T ω`.

results.title: Counting lemma for rank counts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Counting lemma: for any family of reals `t` indexed by `G` and any `k`, at most `k` elements `h` have rank count `#{g | t h ≤ t g}` at most `k`.

results.title: Validity of permutation p-values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Lehmann and Romano (2005), §15.2; Hemerik and Goeman (2018): if the law `μ` is invariant under the action of a finite group `G`, the permutation p-value of any measurable statistic is valid.

results.title: Monte Carlo permutation p-value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Monte Carlo permutation p-value `(1 + #{b | T(g_b • ω) ≥ T(ω)}) / (B + 1)` of the statistic `T` at the data `ω` with the `B` drawn group elements `g`.

results.title: Validity of Monte Carlo permutation p-values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Phipson and Smyth (2010); Hemerik and Goeman (2018): if the null law `μ` is invariant under a finite group `G` and `g₁, …, g_B` are drawn independently and uniformly from `G`, independently of the data, then `(1 + #{b | T(g_b • ω) ≥ T(ω)}) / (B + 1)` is a valid p-value under the joint law.

results.title: Counting `t`-subsets with a prescribed inside and outside
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a finite type with `n` elements, if `A` and `B` are disjoint and `#A ≤ t`, the `t`-subsets that contain `A` and are disjoint from `B` number `(n - #A - #B).choose (t - #A)`. The hypothesis `#A ≤ t` is needed: without it the count is `0` while the truncated right-hand side need not be; see `card_powersetCard_filter_subset_disjoint_eq_ite`.

results.title: Counting `t`-subsets with a prescribed inside and outside, in general
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For arbitrary `A` and `B` in a finite type with `n` elements, the number of `t`-subsets that contain `A` and are disjoint from `B` is `(n - #A - #B).choose (t - #A)` when `A` and `B` are disjoint and `#A ≤ t`, and `0` otherwise.

results.title: Mean edge cut of a uniform `t`-subset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `n` be the number of vertices, `M` the number of edges and `1 ≤ t < n`. The average, over the `n.choose t` subsets `S` with `t` elements, of the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in `S` is `2t(n-t)/(n(n-1)) * M`.

results.title: Sum of the edge cut over all `t`-subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `1 ≤ t`, the numbers of edges of `G` with exactly one endpoint in `S`, summed over the `t`-subsets `S` of the vertices, give `2 * M * (n - 2).choose (t - 1)`, where `M` is the number of edges and `n` the number of vertices.

results.title: Variance of the edge cut of a uniform `t`-subset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `n ≥ 4` be the number of vertices, `M` the number of edges, `S₂ = ∑ v, (G.degree v) ^ 2` and `1 ≤ t < n`. Put `a = 2t(n-t)/(n(n-1))` and `b = 4t(t-1)(n-t)(n-t-1)/(n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3))`. For `S` uniform among the `t`-subsets, the population variance of the cut size `R S = #(G.interedges S Sᶜ)`, written as the average of `(R S - μ) ^ 2` with `μ` the average of `R`, is `b * M + (a / 2 - b) * S₂ + (b - a ^ 2) * M ^ 2`.

results.title: Averaging over an invariant finite group
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the law `μ` is invariant under the action of a finite group `G`, and for `μ`-almost every `ω` exactly `c` group elements `g` move `ω` into the measurable set `A`, then `μ A = c / |G|`. Summing `μ (g⁻¹ • A) = μ A` over `G` turns `|G| μ A` into the integral of the number of such `g`.

results.title: Exact-cardinality subset-sum instances

results.summary: An exact-cardinality subset-sum instance is a triple $(a, K, T)$ consisting of a list $a$ of natural numbers, a natural number $K$ (the cardinality) and a natural number $T$ (the target).

results.title: Feasibility of an exact-cardinality subset-sum instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An exact-cardinality subset-sum instance $(a, K, T)$ is feasible when some subsequence of the list $a$ (entries kept in order, not necessarily contiguous) has exactly $K$ entries and sum $T$.

results.title: Exact-cardinality subset sum as a decision problem

results.title: EXACT-CARDINALITY SUBSET SUM is NP-complete

results.title: Padding a string to a given length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a binary string $p$, the padding of $p$ to length $n$ is the string $0^k 1 p$ with $k = \max(n - 1 - |p|, 0)$; when $|p| < n$ it has length $n$.

results.title: Few strings have small complexity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fewer than `2 ^ m` strings have complexity below `m`. Padding their shortest descriptions to length `m` maps them injectively to strings of length `m` other than `0ᵐ`.

results.title: Binary strings of a given length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the finite set of all binary strings of length $n$.

results.title: Most strings are incompressible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $c$, fewer than $2^{n-c}$ binary strings of length $n$ have Kolmogorov complexity less than $n - c$, where $n - c$ is read as $0$ when $c > n$.

results.title: Incompressible strings exist at every length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Some string of length `n` has complexity at least `n`.

results.title: Kolmogorov complexity is not computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The function sending each binary string $x$ to its Kolmogorov complexity $K(x)$ is not computable: no partial recursive function, acting on binary strings through their encodings as natural numbers, halts on every binary string $x$ with output $K(x)$.

results.title: Lamport public key
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : X \to Y$ and a secret key $sk : \{0, \dots, \ell - 1\} \times \{0, 1\} \to X$, the public key is the map $pk : \{0, \dots, \ell - 1\} \times \{0, 1\} \to Y$ with $pk(i, b) = f(sk(i, b))$.

results.title: Lamport signing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The signature of a message $m \in \{0, 1\}^\ell$ under a secret key $sk : \{0, \dots, \ell - 1\} \times \{0, 1\} \to X$ is $\sigma \in X^\ell$ with $\sigma_i = sk(i, m_i)$ for every position $i < \ell$.

results.title: Lamport verification
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : X \to Y$. A signature $\sigma \in X^\ell$ on a message $m \in \{0, 1\}^\ell$ is valid for a public key $pk : \{0, \dots, \ell - 1\} \times \{0, 1\} \to Y$ when $f(\sigma_i) = pk(i, m_i)$ for every position $i < \ell$.

results.title: Correctness of Lamport signatures
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : X \to Y$. For every secret key $sk : \{0, \dots, \ell - 1\} \times \{0, 1\} \to X$ and every message $m \in \{0, 1\}^\ell$, the Lamport signature of $m$ under $sk$ is valid for $m$ under the public key of $sk$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : X \to Y$. Given a secret key $sk : \{0, \dots, \ell - 1\} \times \{0, 1\} \to X$, a position $(i, b)$ and a value $y \in Y$, the planted public key takes the value $y$ at $(i, b)$ and the value $f(sk(j, c))$ at every other position $(j, c)$.

results.title: Security reduction for Lamport one-time signatures
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : X \to Y$ be a function on a finite nonempty set $X$, let $\ell \ge 1$ be the message length, and let $A$ be a one-time forger whose random coins range over a finite nonempty set $R$. Then the probability that $A$ wins the one-time forgery game against the Lamport scheme built from $f$ is at most $2\ell$ times the probability that the inverter built from $A$ wins the one-wayness game for $f$.

part.title: Sprague–Grundy theorem
api: Uniqueness of the P-positions of a terminating impartial game

results.title: Uniqueness of the P-positions of a terminating impartial game
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $x \to y$ when there is a move from position $x$ to position $y$, and assume there is no infinite sequence of moves $x_0 \to x_1 \to x_2 \to \cdots$. Call a set $P$ of positions stable if no move leads from a position in $P$ to a position in $P$, and absorbing if from every position outside $P$ some move leads to a position in $P$. Then any two stable and absorbing sets of positions are equal.

results.title: Impartial game
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An impartial game consists of a type of positions, a starting position, for each position $p$ a finite set of positions reachable from $p$ in one move, and a rank function assigning a natural number to each position such that every move strictly decreases the rank: if $q$ is reachable from $p$ in one move, then $\mathrm{rank}(q) < \mathrm{rank}(p)$.

results.title: P-positions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In an impartial game $G$, the P-positions are defined by well-founded recursion along moves: a position $p$ is a P-position if and only if no position reachable from $p$ in one move is a P-position. Positions that are not P-positions are called N-positions.

results.title: Sum of impartial games
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sum $G + H$ of two impartial games $G$ and $H$ is the impartial game whose positions are the pairs $(a, b)$ of a position $a$ of $G$ and a position $b$ of $H$, and in which a move changes exactly one component: from $(a, b)$ one may move to $(a', b)$ for any move from $a$ to $a'$ in $G$, or to $(a, b')$ for any move from $b$ to $b'$ in $H$. Its starting position is the pair of the starting positions of $G$ and…

results.title: Nim heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Nim heap of size $n$ is the impartial game whose positions are $0, 1, \dots, n$, whose starting position is $n$, and in which a move from $k$ goes to any $j < k$; the rank of a position is its value.

results.title: Equivalence of impartial games
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two impartial games $G$ and $H$ are equivalent when no third game tells them apart as summands: for every impartial game $K$, the starting position of the sum $G + K$ is a P-position if and only if the starting position of the sum $H + K$ is a P-position. The starting position of a sum is the pair of the starting positions of its summands.

results.title: Recursive characterization of P-positions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In an impartial game $G$, a position $p$ is a P-position if and only if every position reachable from $p$ in one move is not a P-position.

results.title: Sprague–Grundy theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every impartial game $G$ is equivalent to a Nim heap: there is a natural number $n$ such that $G$ is equivalent to the Nim heap of size $n$.
